Dortmund are second in the Bundesliga and are yet to lose in the competition this season.

They defeated Elversberg last time out, and Kovac wants to see a fast start against Gladbach following the international break.

"We can't afford to take any time to get going," added Kovac.

Industry observers note that "There are still eight games left this year. In these games, we want to cement our place at the top of the Bundesliga. The other teams are pushing from behind. We have to be ready right away.

It has been revealed that "The focus is on this game. It's plain and simple: we have to play our next opponent – Gladbach – in a way that ensures we win the game. Positive results build confidence and fuel the hunger for more.".

Borussia Monchengladbach – Joe Scally.

Amid a season of struggles for Gladbach, wing-back Joe Scally has stood out for the Bundesliga's bottom side.

Among defenders in the competition this season, only Anthony Caci (six) has directly contributed to more goals than Scally (five – three goals, two assists).

Borussia Dortmund – Felix Nmecha.

Felix Nmecha scored his second brace of the Bundesliga season before the international break and has already equalled his personal best of four goals from the 2024-25 campaign.

However, Nmecha has scored 13 of his 14 total Bundesliga goals in home matches, with his only away goal coming in Eintracht Frankfurt in January 2026.

MATCH PREDICTION: BORUSSIA DORTMUND WIN.

Dortmund have started a Bundesliga season unbeaten in nine games for only the fourth time, after 2002-03, 2018-19 and 2023-24 – in 2023-24, their first defeat came in their 10th match.

Across two seasons, Dortmund are unbeaten in 11 Bundesliga games, with their last defeat coming against their upcoming opponents Gladbach in early May (0-1 away).

Meanwhile, four points from nine matches is a new club-record low for Gladbach in the Bundesliga.

Of the 18 Bundesliga teams to have managed four points or fewer after nine games in the three-points-per-win era, only six avoided relegation (33%), most recently Mainz in the 2023-24 season.

However, Dortmund have won only one of their last six Bundesliga away games against Gladbach (D1 L4).

Since the start of the 2020-21 season, Dortmund have not lost more Bundesliga away games against any other side, while Gladbach have not celebrated more Bundesliga home wins against any other opponent in that time.

Borussia Monchengladbach – 20.6%.

The report claims that Osimhen’s camp have been made aware of United’s renewed interest.

Published: 03:48 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 07:04 EST, 19 November 2026.

The world has been waiting 13 years for GTA6 and footballers are not immune from the lure and addictive nature of the game.

In fact, top flight players are notorious gamers given their amount of free time after training and Bryan Mbeumo was one of many to share his excitement at the midnight release.

No doubt upcoming Man United boss Mauricio Pochettino would prefer his players to get a solid night's sleep ahead of taking his first training session on Thursday but Mbeumo couldn't resist a late-night session.

He shared the loading screen of the Rockstar game at midnight on his Instagram story with the word 'historic' as the clock ticked into Thursday morning.

It remains to be seen whether Mbeumo stayed up into the early hours playing but an estimated three million UK adults were expected to call in sick or take annual leave to play.

Sleep is vital for athletes to recover and perform at their best and one NBA star even predicted professionals across sports would see their output 'plummet' as a result of GTA's pull.

Bryan Mbeumo shared this picture on his Instagram story at midnight when GTA went live.

Mauricio Pochettino's first morning of training coincides with the release of GTA, played by Mbeumo and plenty of other athletes who looked forward to the late-night release.

According to recent reports, in a previous video clip online, Mbeumo was being interviewed while on his console and revealed he'd pre-ordered the game, saying: 'I'm just waiting now, the game will make me stay at home every single day... after training.'.

Pochettino, who flew on a private jet to Manchester on Wednesday ahead of his first day in the job on Thursday, will no doubt have a keen eye on whether any of his stars are bleary-eyed in training.

The new boss has an incredibly tight turnaround to prepare for the huge clash with rivals Liverpool on Sunday at Anfield, but perhaps the Reds will also be dealing with GTA-mania.

Alexander Isak was asked about the game's release while on international duty with Sweden and admitted: 'Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.'.

A renowned sleep coach for top athletes, Nick Littlehales, has opined on the effects late-night gaming can have.

'They get lost in it, it’s an engaging distraction, and it satisfies their competitive edge, but just like mindlessly scrolling YouTube or social media, you need to put your own filters and blockers in place, otherwise you’ll find yourself doing something ridiculously stupid and playing for hours and hours, hurting your performance,' he told Ozoon.

'We know it’s unrealistic to expect a player to just stop after exactly two hours when they’re in the zone. You have to accept it and ask them: "Are you prepared to sacrifice your nocturnal sleep to be awake and stimulated? Is it worth it?" If they insist on it, we look at scheduling it. Maybe they game late on Tuesdays, Thursdays.

Recent findings suggest that 'You must have these open conversations instead of outright banning late-night gaming. If you just throw the book at them, they end up taking sleeping tablets, using snus, and taking unregulated supplements they don’t understand just so they can cope. When you help them manage their gaming, they usually start to self-regulate.'.

It’s safe to say Bryan Mbeumo is ready for GTA 6. 🤣🤣 pic.twitter.com/skkPM2GYo9.

Conor McGregor announced that he would give employees at various businesses the day off.

People cheer as Grand Theft Auto VI goes live at London gaming venue XP Tavern.

Arsenal's Declan Rice could be another to be locked into the new GTA having previously spoken about how much gaming helps him switch off.

Industry observers note that he told GQ: 'I can never sleep after night games. It’s impossible. I’ll be that wired. I'll play Call of Duty, Grand Theft Auto, FIFA. Anything. Just play with a load of my friends. Adrenaline, everything. You don’t really settle down.

'I feel like when you’re playing at this level, your mind’s just constantly – it’s just going.'.

Football clubs, businesses and even schools are braced for the effects of the newly introduced game, with one head teacher in Chelmsford, Essex, entering students into a raffle to win a £10 Amazon voucher in an attempt to stop them bunking off.

UFC star Conor McGregor revealed that he was giving the day off to 400 employees at his various businesses so they could play the game.

And Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared an image of himself playing the game, flying a helicopter after it was launched.

The astonishing level of anticipation for GTA6 has banked more than £1.14bn in pre-orders alone and is set to become by far the highest grossing game ever made.

It debuted with a score of 99 on review aggregator website Metacritic – equalling 1998's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time as the highest-rated video game ever.

Some 2.8million UK adults are set to play the game on launch day alone, according to a Uswitch poll commissioned earlier this month.

Over in the US, a number of athletes were frank in their honesty about how many of them would be addicted to the game.

Houston Rockets center Steven Adams previously said: 'You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide… GTA is dropping.

Industry observers note that 'So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though.

Sources indicate that 'Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good.'.

🚨🇸🇪 Alexander Isak on the release of GTA 6: “Yeah, so I think it’ll be difficult to reach me from the 19th, when it comes out. I’ll be locked in. That’s the plan.” 😂 pic.twitter.com/LEhQQRo8pQ.

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois shared this image from playing the game.

'I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days,' Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell, a Miami native, said with a grin. 'We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time, You know it's going to be a big one.'.

Plenty of other athletes share Atwell's excitement, but will prioritize their work on the field.

In a recent development, 'I think a lot of athletes are responsible,' remarked Los Angeles Rams offensive lineman Steve Avila. 'But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure.'.

Upcoming York Jets running back Breece Hall concurs: 'Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game,' Hall noted. 'But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun.'.

There were some technological concerns in the hours leading up to the game's release, with the official PlayStation Network status website yesterday acknowledging some players were unable to access online features.

In a recent development, A statement on the website read: 'You might have difficulty launching games, apps, or network features. We're working to resolve the problem as soon as possible. Thank you for your patience.'.

Declan Rice is another star to stay up late gaming as it helps him switch off after significant games.

Those issues appeared to be cleared up by midnight, with PlayStation declaring all of its services were 'up and running' in the hours after the game went live.

BT and EE called the upcoming launch an 'unprecedented gaming download event' because of the size of the game and the number of people expected to play.

The pre-download drove the second-highest broadband traffic peak ever on BT's networks, only beaten by Arsenal v Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in May, and Virgin Media O2 saw its highest-ever daily data volume last Tuesday.

While the exact number of people who have pre-ordered GTA VI is not known, Sony remarked it is the most pre-ordered game in the history of PlayStation Store.

Schools have urged pupils not to use the release of the game – which carries an age rating of 18 – as an excuse to skip lessons.

Sales of gaming consoles and accessories surged in the run-up to launch day.

A man walks past a Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) digital billboard advert in Milan - the game's release has become a global event.

Department store chain John Lewis noted it had seen a 62 per cent year-on-year increase in sales of gaming consoles and accessories, while retailer Currys reported a 149 per cent increase in PlayStation 5 consoles alone.

GTA VI returns to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City, Rockstar's fictional version of Miami, which has featured in previous instalments of the series.

The game follows two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, who find themselves caught up in a criminal conspiracy in the fictional state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.

The pair become embroiled in a Bonnie and Clyde-style crime story after 'an easy score goes wrong', leaving them 'forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive'.

Antonio Conte has played down suggestions he missed out on the Manchester United job because of his demanding reputation in management.

United made their third mid-season managerial change in three years after sacking Michael Carrick with Mauricio Pochettino coming in as his replacement earlier this month.

According to recent reports, conte was among the names initially explored along with Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann. The Italian, a free agent since parting ways with Napoli, was thought to be keen on the role at Old Trafford but it was widely reported United had reservations over some of his methods.

The Italian led Juventus, Chelsea, Inter Milan and Napoli to league titles but has not lasted longer than two seasons at any club since leaving the Bianconeri in 2014.

Conte has a reputation for being hugely demanding with players and the board but in an interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio he insisted anyone scared of his approach is scared of winning.

The coach recalled a meeting with Sir Alex Ferguson during his time in charge of Chelsea, praising the standards the Scot said before insisting the idea United no longer want to meet those standards is ‘offensive’.

‘If someone is scared of my method, then they’re scared of winning, because that methodology leads to winning,’ Conte said.

‘That’s my answer. United has such an important history that it seems strange to imagine anyone being scared of a job aimed at restoring the club to its former glory.

They last won the championship in 2013, under Ferguson. I have enormous respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. I’ve read his book, and when I was in London, I was lucky enough to go to his house and spend a day with him. He’s incredibly eager to talk about football, even if it’s sometimes hard to understand his Scottish accent.

According to recent reports, ‘With his method and his approach, he made Manchester United great. That’s why I find certain words about United almost offensive: it’s like vetoing a return to their own history. The method is needed to achieve notable results.

‘If you then tell me that it’s a method that needs work, I’d say yes: everyone needs to work, not just the players.’.

A snap 24-hour Tube strike that has shut one line and seriously disrupted another is set to affect passengers heading to events in the capital this weekend.

Members of the Transport Salaried Staffs’ Association (TSSA) working on the Piccadilly Line walked out at noon on Friday in a dispute over the dismissal of a colleague.

As a result the Piccadilly Line was closed and on Friday afternoon there was a part closure and severe delays on the District line.

TfL said previously due to the shared infrastructure around the Ealing Common District line depot, there will be no service between Earl’s Court and either Richmond or Ealing Broadway from midday on Friday until Saturday evening, with a reduced service on the rest of the line.

TfL indicates services began to reduce after 10:30 on Friday and will not return to normal on the Piccadilly line until Saturday evening.

The Night Tube will not operate on the Piccadilly line through Friday night. The Night Tube service is expected to operate on Saturday night.

The Elizabeth line, DLR, London Overground, buses and trams are expected to operate as normal during the strike action.

However, these services are likely to be busier than usual as customers seek alternative routes, claims TfL.

Customers travelling to and from Heathrow Airport, as well as those making journeys across central, west and north London, are advised to blueprint ahead and allow extra time for their journeys.

There are also a number of other planned closures on the Tube and Overground that will cause disruption.

There is a busy day of sport in the capital and disruption on public transport will affect the plans of fans heading to the games.

Lulu was at ex-husband John Frieda’s bedside when he died – on her birthday.

Idina Menzel turns heads in extravagant cape ahead of Royal Variety show.

Londoner charged after ‘knives and other weapons’ seized at busy station.

Art After Dark is back with an exciting calendar of cultural events.

Chelsea’s home game against Leeds kicks off at 3pm, with the District line, a popular way of arriving at Stamford Bridge, still expected to be facing severe delays before and after the game.

While fans hoping to use the Piccadilly line as part of their journey to Tottenham Hotspur Stadium to watch the 3pm game between Spurs and against Ipswich Town at the will have to find alternatives, which is likely to make other forms of transport very busy.

District line delays could also hinder rugby fans wanting to use it as part of the journey to Twickenham to watch England vs the All Blacks at the Allianz Stadium.

Visitors to do any venues or destinations along the Piccadilly line may have to rethink how they are going to get to and from their destination.

The walkout will have affected anyone wanting to use the line to reach South Kensington to visit the Royal Albert Hall for the Royal Variety performance on Friday night.

Drake Millington plays the Eventim Apollo in Hammersmith on Friday night, normally easy to reach by Piccadilly or District line.

While others hoping to use the line for a night out in the West End, or visit for Christmas shopping or to see the Christmas lights on Saturday will have to rethink their journeys.

Visitors to Winter Wonderland in Hyde Park may also have to rethink their journeys.

On Saturday and Sunday there will be no service between Queen's Park and Harrow & Wealdstone on the Bakerloo line due to track work.

There will be no service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Lioness line on Saturday or Sunday.

No service between Euston and Watford Junction on the Mildmay line on Sunday, with also no service between Camden Road and Stratford after 10.15pm.

On the Weaver line on Sunday there will be no service oin the entire line until 10.15am.

There will be no service between Stratford International and Canning Town on the DLR on Saturday and Sunday.

It has been revealed that on Sunday, there will be no service on the Elizabeth line between Paddington and Ealing Broadway until 07:45am due to Network Rail maintenance work. There will also be a reduced service between Paddington and Heathrow/Maidenhead.

Lee Stewart, Transport for London’s head of London Underground service control, said: “We are extremely disappointed that TSSA is proceeding with unjustified strike action in response to the dismissal of an employee working a second job while receiving full sick pay.

“We will do all we can to minimise disruption for our customers.

“I would encourage Piccadilly Line customers travelling on Friday and Saturday to check before they travel and consider alternative routes where possible.

“Our teams will be working hard to keep London moving and provide customers with the information they need to plan their journeys.”.

TSSA general secretary Maryam Eslamdoust visited picket lines on Friday, and said: “Our members working in service control on the Piccadilly Line are determined to take industrial action in support of their colleague who has been unfairly treated by London Underground.

Sources indicate that “We don’t take strike action lightly. Everyone here knows what it costs to lose a day’s pay.

“You’ve come out because you know that every London Underground worker deserves a fair hearing when a staffing matter arises.”.

The walkout is not related to plans for a series of strikes by Tube driver members of the Rail, Maritime and Transport union in a separate dispute over shift patterns.

Their first strike will affect the whole network on November 26 and 27.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Virgil van Dijk is unsure where he will be playing his football next season, with his Liverpool contract due to expire in the summer.

The Dutchman, 35, has plied his trade at Anfield since 2018 and is now a two-time Premier League champion.

He will be out of contract in June, though, and has revealed in a upcoming interview with Sky Sports that it remains unclear whether he will extend his stay. He is, however, clear that he expects to continue his playing career for several more years.

Per reports from BBC Sport, talks regarding a new deal are underway but an agreement is not close, and no resolution is expected before the new year. From January, Van Dijk will be free to sign pre-contract agreements with clubs outside England.

“The main thing for me is that I feel good and I'm looking after myself and I still have many more years in my opinion,” stated Van Dijk.

“Whatever's going to happen after this season, we'll see.

“At this moment of time, if anyone notes that or put out that they know what I'm going to do next season, it's untrue because at this moment of time, speaking to you, I've got no idea either.”.

He continued, explaining that he will remain fully focused on on-pitch matters as he awaits clarity on his contract situation.

In a recent development, “But I'm relaxed with it because if you know me, I only focus on what I can control and that's at the moment the Manchester United game. Then we'll focus to the Champions League and whatever happens in the fresh year coming, we'll see then.

"But it's been an incredible journey, almost 10 years this summer and it's been a major part of my life and I'll forever be grateful for anything that happened over those years.”.

He added, matter-of-factly: “If it's getting extended, we'll see then. If not, then I'm going to say goodbyes in the summer.”.

EU moves to loosen rules on pesticide use as experts sound the alarm

📅 22 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1174 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, as part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation.
  • Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.
  • The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation. These include a move to ease rules controlling the use of pesticides and herbicides, which help fight pests and weeds.

Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.

The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default. Safety reviews would only be done in exceptional cases, and regulatory authorities, not the industry, would bear responsibility.

Recent findings suggest that the commission has said its goal is to cut costs, simplify work for authorities and help farmers stay competitive. Scientists and doctors, however, warn that concerns over human health and environmental impact from these toxic substances are being brushed aside.

The European Commission has said it's responding to complaints from farmers and the agriculture industry to clarify EU rules that govern pesticide use.

A joint statement released in May by 19 food associations, including CropLife Europe, which promotes pesticides, said complicated administrative procedures and a lengthy approvals process meant farmers were "left without any effective solutions to protect their crops against insects, weeds and diseases," putting food security and livelihoods at risk.

"The existing system of periodic renewal assessment of every active substance has become unsustainable," the commission's press service told DW, citing "chronic delays" and "bottlenecks" in the approval of new, more sustainable products.

In recent negotiations, EU member states stated open-ended authorizations should be restricted to "low-risk active substances.".

But their stance is still wanting to extend initial approval periods for other substances to up to 15 years, and a maximum of 25 years for renewals.

In a recent development, herbert Dorfmann, a center-right Italian member of the European Parliament, mentioned there is currently a yearslong delay in approving new pesticides, including more eco-friendly options, meaning farmers are forced to rely on older substances. Or, if these are banned, go without altogether.

The commission wants to "make the system more efficient and responsive," while guaranteeing that "the protection of human and animal health and the environment remain the highest priorities.".

Dorfmann, who as co-rapporteur is responsible for interinstitutional negotiations on the glitch, backs the commission's stance, saying the EU needs "to open up the system for innovation.".

He aims to bring the parliament's proposal on the new pesticide rules to a vote among EU lawmakers before the end of the year.

Ecologists and medical experts, however, have spoken out forcefully against the proposed changes, saying the potential implications for human health and the environment are being downplayed.

In September, more than 500 experts from across the EU signed an open letter calling on the European Parliament to suspend its consideration of the new regulations and conduct an independent investigation into health and environmental impacts.

On October 7, UN rights experts also backed the call for a full review into whether the proposed changes violated the EU's obligations under international human rights law, especially with regard to agricultural workers and children.

It has been revealed that pesticides can persist in the environment, contaminating water and degrading soils. They can also drive biodiversity loss and poison other animals higher up the food chain.

When it comes to humans, the European Environment Agency has mentioned it was "not yet possible to estimate the burden of disease linked to current levels of exposure to all pesticides.".

However, exposure to chemical pesticides, including banned substances that still persist in the environment, has been linked to various cancers, chronic respiratory disease, neurological disorders and developmental delays, as well as problems with fertility and behavior.

And exposure is widespread: A survey conducted between 2014 and 2021 found that 84% of urine samples from both children and adults in five European countries contained residue from two or more pesticides.

Martina Vijver, scientific director and ecotoxicology expert at Leiden University in the Netherlands, noted experts were "deeply concerned" that the EU's current proposal "will weaken rather than strengthen the level of protection for pesticide regulation.".

Speaking at the European Parliament in September, she mentioned regular reassessments were key to evaluating the safety of pesticides with new findings, pointing out that the perception of risk changes over time.

"The regulatory system must remain capable of correcting yesterday's decisions with tomorrow's knowledge," she remarked.

Salome Roynel, a policy officer at the Pesticide Action Network Europe, an NGO based in Brussels, said the harmful effects of pesticides aren't often fully understood until years later, when the product is up for reconsideration.

"New science emerges all the time," she told DW, highlighting how 56 active substances have been banned in the EU since 2011 as a result of periodic reviews.

That includes the insecticide chlorpyrifos, previously used in orchards and on vegetable and cereal crops, which has been tied to harmful effects on children's brain development.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel stated it was "obvious that there was some kind of alignment" between the changes proposed by the EU institutions and the demands of the pesticide lobby.

This echoes a new report by nonprofit research and campaign group Corporate Europe Observatory, which noted Dorfmann and other lawmakers had "copy-pasted […] industry demands" into their regulatory proposals.

Dorfmann denied the lobby influence, telling DW he had met with "both sides, industry and environmental associations," in public debates on the concern.

"The main objective is not to keep old products in the market. The main objective is to bring fresh ones to the market," Dorfmann said.

Part of that strategy, he added, would be to help more environmentally friendly "biocontrol" products and low-risk substances to bypass current administrative hurdles and get on the market faster.

It's an idea previously championed by Vijver, who agrees that the current system means more environmentally friendly pesticides are stuck in an administrative "traffic jam." She told DW that biocontrol products could go in a green "bus lane" to ease the way to approval at the European Food Safety Authority, while maintaining crucial safety reviews to filter out the more dangerous products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel also supports the initiative to speed up approval for biocontrol substances, but mentioned it needs to be part of a wider system change that includes financial support, monitoring and training to use these upcoming products, as well as maintaining the restrictions on more harmful chemical pesticides ― not further deregulation.

"If farmers get easier access to synthetic pesticides tomorrow, they would have no incentive to switch to biocontrol," she said. "It's key to put [biocontrol pesticides] on the market and we fully support that, but… it will not be the silver bullet.".

Mikel Arteta revealed Arsenal defender William Saliba is "in good condition" and could feature against Newcastle United on Saturday.

Saliba is yet to play for the Arsenal first team this season after suffering a back injury during France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain in the summer.

In the 2025-26 campaign, when Arsenal won their first Premier League title in 22 years and reached the Champions League final, Saliba won possession more often than any other Gunners defender (177).

The Frenchman also won the second-most duels (198), won the third-most tackles (35) and recorded the third-most interceptions (29).

Roberto De Zerbi has revealed that James Maddison is still suffering from the same hip problem he sustained during pre-season.

The Tottenham midfielder has started just two games in all competitions this season and has not featured since coming off injured midway through Spurs’ 2-0 victory over Chelsea last month.

Maddison is available for selection against Ipswich this weekend and was also named in the matchday squad in each of Spurs’ last two league games against Crystal Palace and Leeds.

However, De Zerbi’s decision not to bring him off the bench against Palace or Leeds has raised concerns that Maddison is still not fully fit.

The 29-year-old returned from an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury at the end of last season, and he had hoped to use pre-season to build his way back to full fitness and force his way into De Zerbi’s starting lineup.

Maddison’s summer was, however, disrupted by setbacks, with a hip glitch restricting his ability to train or play with the rest of the squad, and De Zerbi has now revealed that, four months into the season, the same problem is continuing to hamper the England playmaker.

In a recent development, “After Chelsea he had the same injury he felt in the Chelsea game and not a major injury but he was not able to work. He had a problem with his hip,” De Zerbi stated in his pre-match press conference on Friday afternoon.

“It’s not a major problem, but if you don’t work consistently, you lose the physical condition, and to play in this level of competition you have to stay in the top physical condition.

“He is still young, 29 years is not old, and he has to push and demand of himself the top in terms of physical condition, because if he is 80 or 90 per cent of his physical condition he makes the difference for us, he changes the games.”.

Maddison, who has been unable to train consistently this season, saw his professionalism called into question after Spurs’ defeat to Leeds earlier this month when pictures surfaced of him drinking with friends.

The incident in question occurred on the first of three days off for Spurs’ first-team squad, and De Zerbi indicates he has no issues with Maddison’s conduct, instead joking that he was “very angry” that he was not invited.

#37496. Breaking: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • Sources indicate that the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

They only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

Sources indicate that the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, says she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

In a recent development, "That's the bad news," noted marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

According to recent reports, underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

It has been revealed that around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

According to recent reports, "Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," stated Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

But the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

Through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

According to recent reports, "Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he said.

Recent findings suggest that the collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

"We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig said.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing new ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

Recent findings suggest that "Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she remarked.

"The big advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar mentioned they currently "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

Thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

They then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the new crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

"We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen mentioned. "It's looking really good.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England captain Harry Kane is facing three months out with an ankle injury, Bayern Munich boss Vincent Kompany has confirmed.

The Ballon d’Or winner scored against both Croatia and Spain in the international break and was seeking a first goal in five matches for the Bundesliga leaders in all competitions at the Allianz Arena.

However, as he looked to latch on to Michael Olise’s deflected low cross at the back post, Cologne full-back Joel Schmied got to the ball first and clattered into Kane’s left leg in his follow-through.

Kane immediately clutched his lower leg and writhed in pain for a few moments before gingerly getting back to his feet, but he was a virtual bystander for the next couple of minutes.

The 33-year-old gestured to the dugout, sunk to the turf and then received treatment on his ankle before making way for Tom Bischof, limping off the field alongside two physios.

Kane had a quick exchange with Kompany, back in the Bayern hot-seat for the first time in six matches after being diagnosed with meningeal irritation last month, before heading down the tunnel.

Speaking at full-time, Kompany confirmed Kane was facing months on the sidelines with what Max Eberl described as a tear of the syndesmotic ligament.

Sky Germany has reported he can expect to spend three months on the sidelines, meaning he will hope return before England face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March.

Matters only grew worse for Bayern thereafter, as Olise was also forced off shortly after Kane with an ankle injury of his own. He was able to walk off the pitch before treatment, though.

Tottenham loanee Mikey Moore opened the scoring for Cologne after just 12 minutes, but the match finished 1-1 as Nathaniel Brown equalised for the hosts before the break.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.

Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s fresh head coach.

United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.

They show that United brought in total revenues of £146.1m compared to £140.3m in the first quarter last year, but made an operating loss for the quarter of £3m compared with an operating profit of £13m 12 months ago.

The results come just weeks after co-owner Avram Glazer told a conference that the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

Sources say that United acted early in the season to address the drop in form under Carrick that saw United slide into the relegation zone, and the club are now focused on improving results under Pochettino.

The Argentine is expected to be given a modest transfer budget in January to make new signings, with United in the market for a striker, left-back and centre-back.

Man United's latest financial results come after the Glazers said that success isn't dependent on results.

The results don't include the £10m United paid to buy Pochettino and his staff from the US national team.

It has been revealed that chief executive Omar Berrada mentioned: ‘Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably. We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.’.

In a recent development, the latest results only cover the first five Premier League fixtures of the season, one Champions League match and the League Cup defeat to Brighton. Sources insist that they show the benefit of the cost-cutting under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos and what they say is improved operational efficiency.

United have reiterated their guidance of total revenues of £740-£760m for this financial year after reporting that the first quarter saw rises in broadcast (£5.3m), retail (£1.3m) and matchday (£0.6m) revenues.

However, sponsorship revenue was down by £1.4m despite a new training kit deal with Betway, largely due to United playing individual pre-season friendlies rather than going on summer tour.

Employee benefit expenses for the quarter were £79.9m, an increase of £6.3m due mainly to players' wages going up 25 per cent after qualifying for the Champions League.

United's borrowing has increased 19 per cent from a year ago, with the club's historic US dollar debt up $125m to $775m 'as a result of the refinancing of our senior secured notes in June 2026'.

This rise, which was revealed in the last set of results in September, equates to £577.4m, up from £481.2m. The net cost of financing that debt dropped from £21.4m to £14.5m.

Meanwhile, United’s borrowing on the club's revolving credit facility was £207.1m as of September 30, down from £268m a year ago.

Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 47 min read (9480 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~47 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing1.
  • Sources indicate that integrated photonic devices have emerged as a powerful platform for the next-generation information technologies, and the development of efficient and scalable integrated photonic circuits has become a central focus of state-of-the-art research.
  • According to recent reports, however, the effectiveness of all-optical devices depends critically on the ability to harness optical nonlinearities.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing1. Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses2. Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms3,4,5. However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

Sources indicate that integrated photonic devices have emerged as a powerful platform for the next-generation information technologies, and the development of efficient and scalable integrated photonic circuits has become a central focus of state-of-the-art research. Photonics enables ultrafast signal propagation, low-loss transport, broadband modulation and highly efficient information processing6,7. In this context, it is crucial that the same architecture supports a variety of integrated components, including on-chip coherent light sources, frequency-comb generators, modulators, amplifiers and switches, enabling coherent phase manipulation of propagating optical fields as a key functionality for dynamical reconfigurability and interferometric-based operations.

According to recent reports, however, the effectiveness of all-optical devices depends critically on the ability to harness optical nonlinearities. As conventional platforms based on linear dielectric materials or lithium niobate (LiNbO3) show intrinsically weak nonlinear responses8,9, structures supporting exciton–polaritons have been proposed as an effective alternative. These hybrid light–matter excitations, formed under non-perturbative radiation coupling between excitons and purely photonic eigenmodes, combine photon-like propagation with strong optical nonlinearities, making them attractive for ultrafast all-optical information processing10,11,12,13. Although exciton–polaritons have been extensively studied in vertically confined microcavities, planar architectures such as polariton waveguides14,15,16,17 have recently attracted increasing interest owing to their ability to confine light within smaller modal volumes, thereby enhancing exciton–photon coupling, increasing polariton group velocities and facilitating on-chip integration. When combined with suitable active materials showing large exciton binding energies, polariton operation can be sustained at room temperature5, a condition fulfilled by perovskites, which stand out for their exceptional and tunable optoelectronic properties and ease of processing, eliminating the demanding fabrication procedures typically required for conventional semiconductors. In addition, their strong polariton nonlinearities, comparable to that of gallium arsenide (GaAs)-based systems, makes them an increasingly attractive platform for polariton-based applications at room temperature18,19,20,21. However, fabricating high-quality perovskite photonic components remains challenging because well-defined edges and smooth surfaces are essential for achieving satisfactory performance22,23,24, whereas conventional postprocessing often degrades the crystal morphology and optical quality. Despite recent progress, efficient in-coupling and out-coupling of light remains a main bottleneck. In particular, the realization of coherent on-chip tunable light sources, optical amplification of propagating polariton signals and efficient nonlinear phase control—only partially explored in planar microcavities under cryogenic conditions25 and still absent in guided propagating polariton systems—remains a key outstanding challenge. Overcoming these limitations is crucial to achieving robust, room-temperature, scalable and fully integrated nonlinear photonic devices.

In a recent development, here we address these critical challenges by developing a fully integrated perovskite-based polaritonic circuit in which waveguides and grating couplers are simultaneously defined within the active materials using an innovative bottom-up soft-lithographic strategy that combines surface-tension-assisted and microfluidic growth processes26,27,28. This growth approach eliminates the need for any subsequent postprocessing, enabling the direct integration of hundreds-of-micrometres-long, micrometre-wide caesium lead bromide (CsPbBr3) waveguides with subwavelength gratings featuring tunable periodicity and filling factors. Under off-resonant pumping, the integrated gratings provide longitudinal optical feedback, enabling polariton lasing in an in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavity, with emission efficiently propagating along the waveguide and readily tunable by means of the grating geometry. We also demonstrate efficient optical amplification in a two-beam experiment, in which a resonantly injected propagating polariton wavepacket is amplified through stimulation from the exciton reservoir created by an extra off-resonant beam. The threshold-like amplification resembles key features of spiking neurons, offering a promising route towards the development of neuromorphic polariton devices29,30. In parallel, we achieve nonlinear optical phase control of propagating polariton signals, enabling interferometric functionalities with phase shifts reaching 2π. Our results demonstrate room-temperature polaritonic circuits with active nonlinear functionalities, marking an notable step towards ultra-compact, highly nonlinear polariton devices for integrated photonics and optical information processing.

Industry observers note that csPbBr3 perovskite waveguides with various geometries were directly fabricated on glass substrates using a modified soft-lithography approach that combines surface-tension-driven lithography with microfluidic processing from a liquid precursor solution, following the procedure sketched in Fig. 1a and detailed in the Methods (Supplementary Figs. 1–4). The process uses a patterned polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) replica moulded from a silicon master (Fig. 1b), yielding the perovskite waveguides with integrated gratings shown in Fig. 1c–e. This hybrid method enables the direct formation of hierarchical architectures through controlled self-assembly under saturation conditions and controlled temperature, yielding micrometre-scale waveguides decorated with integrated nanometric grating arrays. The soft-lithography route overcomes key limitations of conventional fabrication by exploiting elastomeric replication, enabling a simple, low-temperature and non-destructive process. It eliminates the need for multi-step lithography, avoids postprocessing damages and refractive-index mismatches, while significantly reducing fabrication cost and time.
