Lorient will aim to extend a superb run against their Breton neighbours Rennes, who make the short trip to the Stade du Moustoir on Sunday afternoon.

Sitting 10th in the Ligue 1 table on 15 points from 10 outings (W4, D3, L3), the hosts trail the eighth-placed visitors by a single point, with the Red and Blacks themselves just one adrift of sixth-placed Nice.

Lorient go into the derby in good heart, having taken three wins, a draw and a loss from their last five league fixtures while keeping four shutouts, which lifts their tally to a division-high six this season.

Alexandre Dujeux’s team bounced back from a disappointing loss against Brest on home soil by securing 2-0 victory away at Le Havre before the international break, thanks to strikes from Isaak Toure and Jean-Victor Makengo.

That success was only the second time all season that the Morbihan side have netted more than once in a match, in a campaign shaped by a cautious approach that has produced a league-low 17 goals across their fixtures.

Lorient’s tally of nine strikes in Ligue 1 this term is the joint-poorest in the top flight, alongside two of the bottom three sides in Angers and Le Havre, though only Lille (seven) have shipped fewer than the Merlus’ eight.

Recent findings suggest that interestingly, three-quarters of those eight concessions have come at Stade du Moustoir, where both of their wins from five games (D1. L2) season have arrived with a clean sheet, so another watertight showing would be crucial on Sunday.

Even so, Lorient can approach the contest with belief, having beaten Rennes in each of the past six meetings, including a 6-0 aggregate triumph across both league encounters in 2025-26, four of those goals arriving at home.

That makes this a daunting assignment for the visitors, who have lost three of their last five in the French top flight (W2), and went down 2-1 at home to Les Dogues in their most recent outing.

Franck Haise’s team briefly led Ligue 1 after a 3-0 win over Strasbourg in October, but subsequent defeats by Nice and Lille mean they have collected only one victory from six games in all competitions.

In Europe, however, Rennes are unbeaten through four fixtures this term, having drawn the last two, and sit 17th in the Europa League standings ahead of a Matchday 5 trip to NEC next Thursday, once this Brittany derby is done.

There is little doubt that Haise’s charges boast a greater attacking threat than this weekend’s hosts, having scored 21 times in the league, but their defensive record has been a major worry, with the same number shipped, which is more than any side in the top half.

The Red and Blacks have also struggled on their travels, losing each of their last three away games in Ligue 1 and conceding at least four times in every one, a run that is worth bearing in mind when comparing goals markets at the best fresh betting sites UK.

Right wing-back Panos Katseris also remains unavailable because of a muscle complaint that has kept him out since September, while midfielder Bandiougou Fadiga is back in training after a hamstring problem and could be in contention.

Ibrahima Balde is fit again after recovering from an Achilles injury, although Souleymane Mame Faye could still be deployed in a two-man support act alongside Makengo behind striker Mamadou Kone.

For the visitors, right-back Przemyslaw Frankowski is doubtful after leaving the Poland camp over the international break with a muscular strain.

Rennes are, however, boosted  by the return of leading marksman Esteban Lepaul, who has netted seven times in the league and could spearhead the attack beside Boulaye Dia after shaking off an ankle issue.

How Berlin's Arab queers are building their community

📅 03 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (770 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • "Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.
  • It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture.
  • Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"Adira" is an Arabic slang term used in Levantine queer culture to describe someone with a strong presence — someone powerful and accomplished.

It is also the name of a Berlin-based collective that curates events and club nights celebrating the diversity of queer Arab* culture. The asterisk signals the inclusion of non-Arab ethnic minorities and people with diverse identities and roots in Southwest Asia and North Africa.

Among the collective's events is the ADIRA Drag Festival, which celebrated its third edition in Berlin in late October.

This year's theme, "Who's Your Diva?!," brought together drag performers paying tribute to legendary figures from across the Eastern Mediterranean who have become queer icons — from Egyptian music legend Umm Kulthum to Turkish star Bülent Ersoy and Lebanese pop icon Haifa Wehbe.

Hassandra, co-founder of ADIRA and the ADIRA Drag Festival, was among the performers, taking on the persona of Lebanese pop star Elissa.

"It is very important for me to bring my Lebanese Arab identity and culture into what I do, because I think it's a very beautiful culture. And there's a lot of campy, glamorous, beautiful divas," Hassandra stated.

Elissa's "whole discography is very romantic, raw, soft, kind of like very Adele vibes," Hassandra told DW ahead of the October 30 show. "However, her personality is known to be the extreme opposite. She's very feisty. Very blunt, very unfiltered. Not soft at all as a person.".

The star is also known for speaking out on political issues in Lebanon. She has publicly voiced support for LGBTQ+ communities in the Middle East, while also frequently sparking controversy across the Arab world with her outspoken positions on other political issues.

Hassandra's ADIRA Drag Festival performance addresses this complexity, ultimately "tapping into her sort of controversial political opinions," the drag artist explained.

This reflects one of the ideas Hassandra hopes to promote with the theme of this year's festival. "As queer people, we tend to idealize a lot of pop divas. But these pop divas are very imperfect in their nature," Hassandra stated. The show provides an opportunity to critically revisit these divas' legacy through a more critical lens.

Industry observers note that "And this sort of critical lens can be taken into the outside world, as in: never follow anyone in life blindly. No one should follow any politician, any political party, any pop diva, any activist blindly.".

Born in Beirut in 1994, Hassandra studied theater and stage acting at the Lebanese University before moving to Berlin in 2017. "I would say it was it was just a very sort of impulsive decision at the age of 22. I mean, there's no doubt that the economic situation was really bad in Lebanon and continued to become even worse," the artist noted.

In Berlin, Hassandra became increasingly involved in the city's independent art scene and queer nightlife. Drag emerged as another form of self-expression for the actor.

Through performances that combine theatrical intensity, political humor, grotesque aesthetics and moments of tenderness, Hassandra challenges conventional understandings of gender and identity.

Recent findings suggest that their work explores themes of home, nostalgia, displacement and queer Arab culture. These ideas are also central to ADIRA, which Hassandra founded in 2023 with Syrian-German DJ and cultural producer Zuher Jazmati, also known as xanax_attax.

Through panel discussions, performances and music events, ADIRA fosters collective participation and community-building.

As Islamophobia and homophobia rise alongside the far right, spaces like ADIRA offer a sense of belonging and support for Arab queer communities.

That sense of community has become even more important following the deadly Islamist terrorist attack during Berlin's Christopher Street Day pride parade in July.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In the aftermath, Hassandra felt caught between their different identities. As an Arab queer person, "you fall in this position where then you start receiving a lot of racism," they mentioned.

In a recent development, "And I think this is why it's notable, for us queer Arabs, to say we are sad over what happened, but that we also reject any of the racism that comes from that," Hassandra said. "I think we [the Arab community] are being used in a lot of ways as a punching bag for a lot of things that are happening.".

In a recent development, rather than allowing the attack to fuel hatred and racism, Hassandra stated, "we should make Germany a safer place for everyone to live in."  "There's place for everyone. It's a huge country," they added.

The interview with Hassandra was conducted by Gönna Ketels.

Augsburg's WWK Arena will be the backdrop for their clash with Mainz 05 on Sunday in a potentially pivotal clash in the battle against relegation.

The home side are 14th in the Bundesliga table with nine points, whereas their opponents are 12th with 10, and a loss for either could leave them in the bottom three.

Augsburg are only two points above 16th-placed Union Berlin, who occupy the relegation playoff spot, while they are just three points ahead of 17th-placed Schalke 04.

The hosts are winless in their past seven league matches, a period in which they claimed just three points and suffered four defeats.

Head coach Manuel Baum will not be pleased that his team conceded at least two goals in six of those fixtures, though he will highlight that the club netted 13 times in that stretch.

Fuggerstadter have played five contests at WWK Arena in 2026-27, and they have triumphed once, drawn three times and won once at the stadium.

Two of those stalemates came against Bayern Munich and Bayer Leverkusen, while their only defeat at home came against third-placed Freiburg at the end of October.

The visitors come into the clash looking to avoid a fifth consecutive loss in all competitions, and avoid losing a fourth straight Bundesliga game.

Perhaps the saving grace for Mainz is that the rest of the bottom seven play teams presently in the top eight, meaning it is unlikely that they will end the weekend in the relegation zone.

Urs Fischer's side did score four goals in their four losses, but they conceded on 11 occasions, and their latest defeat saw them ship twice when they lost 2-1 against Bayern Munich on November 7.

Mainz's record on the road has been largely positive this term, as while they were beaten 4-1 by Elversberg on October 30, they did emerge as winners in their first three away Bundesliga outings of the campaign.

The club are also unbeaten in their five most recent meetings with Augsburg, claiming victory four times, including when they won 2-0 in February.

Mainz 05 form (all competitions):.

Juma Bah, Jeffrey Gouweleeuw and Yannik Keitel could be trusted together in defence, while Robin Fellhauer and Fabian Rieder may start in a double pivot.

Striker Michael Gregoritsch has scored five times in the league this season, and he is certain to lead the line, supported by Anton Kade and Alexis Claude-Maurice.

Though Mainz only have to contend with the absence of centre-back Dominik Kohr, he is not scheduled to return until January because of an ankle injury.

Stefan Posch, Fabio Gruber and Kacper Potulski are likely candidates to start in the team's back three, and the trio may be protected by Paul Nebel and Kaishu Sano from midfield.

From rotten food to political opponents: Researchers explore how disgust relates to our beliefs, and why the connection is complicated

📅 26 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1053 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.
  • But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?
  • Recent findings suggest that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Some studies have linked disgust sensitivity to socially conservative attitudes.

But as Americans vote in the US midterm elections, it's time to think about how disgust shapes our politics, or whether our beliefs shape what we find disgusting?

Recent findings suggest that the smell of rotten food can make us recoil. Certain sexual practices can provoke a similar reaction. And in today's polarized political climate, even political opponents can become objects of disgust.

Psychologists have long investigated whether sensitivity to disgust helps explain political beliefs. A review of 24 studies found that people who reported being more easily disgusted tended to hold more socially conservative views.

One explanation begins with evolution.

"We think that it evolved in part to reduce exposure to things that could make you sick," psychologist Yoel Inbar, of the University of British Columbia in Canada, told DW.

Recent findings suggest that but disgust is not a single emotion. The Three-Domain Disgust Scale, developed in 2009, distinguishes three types:.

One theory is that people who are especially wary of germs and disease may also prefer traditional social rules.

Inbar explains that avoiding potential sources of infection can also mean missing out on new experiences.

"Some people are more on the cautious conservative side, and some people are more on the exploring risk-taking side when it comes to pathogen exposure," he mentioned.

In a recent development, indeed, the language of contamination also appears in political rhetoric. During his 2024 presidential campaign, Donald Trump repeatedly described immigrants as "poisoning the blood of our country." Trump has also described himself as a "germaphobe.".

Inbar acknowledges that the evidence linking sensitivity to disgust with conservative political beliefs remains uncertain.

In a recent development, "We have hypotheses. I don't know that we have as strong of evidence as I would like," Inbar said.

Disgust is not exclusively conservative. And what people find revolting can depend on their values.

A 2020 study titled "Is Disgust a "Conservative" Emotion?" found that liberals and conservatives were disgusted by different things.

Conservatives, generally aligned with the Republicans in US politics, reported greater disgust at examples involving sexual behaviors and drug use, while liberals, generally aligned with the Democrats, reported greater disgust at animal abuse and environmental pollution.

However, when asked how easily disgusted they were in general, there was no clear difference across the political spectrum.

Some early studies suggested conservatives revealed stronger physical reactions to frightening or disgusting images, measured partly through changes in sweating.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

But subsequent research, including a 2020 study by political psychologist Bert Bakker at the University of Amsterdam, struggled to reproduce those findings.

Studies based on questionnaires, however, have generally found that people with more conservative attitudes report being more easily disgusted.

"If bodily reactions don't differ across political groups, why do feelings?" Manos Tsakiris, of Royal Holloway and the Centre for the Politics of Feelings at the University of London, told DW.

Tsakiris and colleague Mariana von Mohr wondered whether the answer might lie in how people perceive and interpret signals from their bodies.

Scientists call the perception of internal sensations, such as hunger, breathing or a racing heart, "interoception." It's sometimes called our eighth sense, alongside the familiar five, plus our senses of balance and body position.

"A bodily signal doesn't arrive with a label attached," Tsakiris told DW. "We have to notice it and make sense of it.".

The researchers surveyed 632 US adults, asking how much they noticed and trusted signals from their bodies — a measure known as "interoceptive sensibility.".

They found that people who were more easily disgusted by sexual behavior tended to be more conservative, regardless of how aware they felt of their bodies.

But for moral disgust, the link to conservatism was found only among people who reported lower bodily awareness.

What particularly surprised Tsakiris was that perceived bodily awareness alone had no link to political views.

"People who are highly attuned to their bodies were neither more liberal nor more conservative," he stated.

Inbar questions whether all forms of disgust are equally useful for studying political attitudes.

He and Joshua Tybur, one of the creators of the Three-Domain Disgust Scale, generally prefer measuring pathogen disgust — reactions to potential sources of disease — rather than sexual disgust.

Questions about sexual disgust may already reflect conservative beliefs about sex.

"It's almost asking people the same thing twice," Inbar noted.

The new study found no significant link between pathogen disgust and conservative views.

Inbar wants the findings on bodily awareness and disgust tested again, with predictions set out in advance. For now, he considers them "suggestive at best.".

Tsakiris suggests that people who struggle to understand their bodily feelings may be more vulnerable to political messages telling them what those feelings mean.

According to recent reports, "I know what you're feeling. You're feeling angry or you're feeling disgusted about this thing," he said, illustrating how someone might put an emotional label on another person's unease.

Such labels could influence political behavior, he argues, although the study did not directly test this.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

"This is how disgust can do political work: it can turn moral judgments about individuals into judgments about whole groups," he said.

The research cannot establish whether disgust shapes political beliefs or existing beliefs shape what people find disgusting. Bakker notes that political beliefs can influence how people describe their own personalities, suggesting the relationship could work both ways.

"Voting behavior is very complex and citizens make up their mind about politics in a complex way," he told DW.

It has been revealed that inbar also cautions against exaggerating disgust's importance. "The thing to emphasize in your story is that the relationship, while it's consistent, is quite small," he stated.

"It's one of the many influences on people's politics.".

Tsakiris advocates what he calls "critical feeling": questioning our emotional responses to provocative material, including social media posts, just as we question the information itself.

He also emphasizes discussing our feelings with others and listening to different perspectives, even when we disagree.

"Life and politics and democracy is a contact sport," he said. Edited by: Rosalie Delaney.

Carlos Forbs is gunning to be Portugal's fresh full-time No7 after Cristiano Ronaldo's retirement - and his audition against Wales went swimmingly.

Ronaldo held the shirt for 20 years, having inherited it from the legendary Luis Figo.

Industry News: Mikel Arteta shuts down Arsenal team news loophole exposed by Christos Tzolis

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.
  • Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).
  • The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 20 Nov 2026 18:48.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that new measures have been introduced to prevent players from accidentally revealing confidential team news through Fantasy Premier League (FPL).

The decision follows an incident involving Christos Tzolis, whose selections in the popular fantasy football game offered an unexpected insight into his availability ahead of Arsenal's Premier League victory over Liverpool earlier this month.

According to The Athletic, Arsenal players have been banned from selecting themselves or their teammates in their FPL squads, reducing the risk of injuries and potential starting line-ups being disclosed before official announcements.

Arteta confirmed the intervention during Friday's press conference ahead of Saturday's trip to Newcastle United, stressing that protecting information about his squad was essential to maintaining trust within the club.

The development is particularly interesting given that Sports Mole was among the outlets to highlight Tzolis's revealing Fantasy Premier League decisions before Arsenal's visit to Anfield on November 1.

Tzolis had been sidelined for approximately a month with a hamstring injury, missing six consecutive Arsenal matches before the trip to Liverpool.

Although Arteta had confirmed that the Greek international had returned to training, his involvement at Anfield remained uncertain.

However, the winger provided a significant indication of his fitness through his own Fantasy Premier League account.

Tzolis transferred himself into his team and selected himself as captain, effectively doubling the points he would earn if he made a successful return.

The decision attracted attention because fantasy managers generally avoid selecting injured players, particularly when using the captaincy on an individual who might not feature.

Sports Mole had already identified the potential significance of those choices in its November 1 report on Tzolis's Fantasy Premier League injury clues.

The same report noted that the former Norwich City winger had retained Riccardo Calafiori in his fantasy squad despite the defender also facing questions over his fitness.

Both players subsequently started at Anfield, where Arsenal secured a 1-0 victory.

Tzolis's activity attracted further attention in the following gameweek.

Ahead of Arsenal's home meeting with Hull City on November 7, the 24-year-old reportedly activated his wildcard, allowing him to make unlimited transfers, and removed every Arsenal player from his fantasy team.

Among those transferred out were Tzolis himself, Calafiori and Ezri Konsa.

Those decisions did not establish who would or would not start against Hull, but they demonstrated how closely players' fantasy activity could be monitored for potential clues.

Tzolis has also previously spoken openly about his enthusiasm for the game.

After Arsenal's opening-day victory over Coventry City, he discussed the points he had accumulated through his own performance, revealing that he had selected himself as captain.

What initially appeared to be a harmless aspect of the player's enjoyment of football has now prompted a response from his manager.

Asked whether he had addressed the matter with his players, Arteta confirmed that discussions had taken place involving Tzolis and other members of the squad.

"With Christos, with the squad and with my kids as well," the Arsenal manager stated.

According to recent reports, "They're constantly asking me about this as well, because they want to know. It's a topic.".

Arteta acknowledged that the popularity of Fantasy Premier League had created a relatively latest challenge for clubs seeking to protect information about their players.

"These are the kind of things that are happening in our society right now," he explained.

Sources indicate that "It's something upcoming. We haven't dealt with it before and we need to put new things in place.".

The Spaniard then emphasised the importance of maintaining confidentiality within the dressing room and coaching staff.

"The confidentiality is something critical because it's about trust and what you're trying to do, and that should be kept as a huge secret.".

Arteta added that measures would be taken to prevent further incidents and subsequently confirmed that restrictions were already in place.

The reported policy does not prevent Arsenal players from participating in Fantasy Premier League altogether.

Instead, it specifically targets the selection of Arsenal footballers in their own fantasy teams, limiting the possibility that transfers or captaincy choices reveal information unavailable to opponents and supporters.

Arsenal are not the first Premier League club to confront the problem.

Chelsea faced similar concerns in October after fantasy accounts associated with players and staff appeared to offer clues about Joao Pedro's injury before his absence against Tottenham Hotspur became public.

The Brazilian had reportedly been removed from several fantasy teams ahead of that fixture, prompting speculation about his availability.

Chelsea subsequently warned staff about the risks of revealing confidential information through the game.

For Arsenal, the problem is especially relevant as Arteta attempts to maintain his side's position at the top of the Premier League.

The Gunners travel to Newcastle on Saturday with a five-point advantage over their nearest challengers, and the manager will be keen to avoid giving opponents unnecessary information about his selection decisions.

Tzolis's fantasy activity may have provided an early indication of his return against Liverpool, but Arsenal's fresh restrictions are designed to ensure that future team news emerges through official channels rather than virtual football transfers.

Could AI give NFTs a second chance?

📅 04 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that remember the NFT boom of 2021?
  • What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.
  • In a recent development, in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that remember the NFT boom of 2021? The surge in trading of non-fungible tokens (NFTs), which are unique, blockchain-recorded digital assets, was one of the stranger economic offshoots of the COVID-19 pandemic.

What started as a marginal curiosity became a highly lucrative sector worth close to $40 billion (€36 billion) globally by the end of 2021, almost as valuable as the global art market itself.

In a recent development, in the highly publicized bust that followed, many NFTs lost practically all their value. The wider cryptocurrency crash was particularly punishing for digital collectibles and largely, they have not recovered.

Industry observers note that the sector is worth up to 97% less than it was at its height in January 2022, and sales continue to plummet. So far this year, total global sales of NFTs are less than $2 billion, according to FindWeb3, a cryptocurrency and blockchain jobs platform. That's more than 90% down from the peaks of 2021 and 2022.

In a recent development, does that mean that NFTs will ultimately fade away to nothing, proving right those who dismissed them as a worthless fad? Or is there still some kind of future for them?

"NFTs will still exist, but it will be a niche collectible market," Ben Charoenwong, associate professor of finance at the business school INSEAD, said. "This doesn't mean there cannot be booms here and there, but certainly not take off as people had imagined in the past.".

He thinks whatever future it can have will be "narrow" and says doubt is growing over the value of "non-fungible" as a concept. Non-fungible means an asset is unique and cannot be traded like for like, whereas fungible means it can be traded like for like, for example, with money.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

He notes that the recent trend of financial institutions converting real-world financial assets, such as bonds and stocks, into digital tokens recorded on a blockchain — the so-called tokenization boom — mostly relates to fungible assets.

However, Andrea Barbon, a finance professor at the University of St Gallen in Switzerland, thinks part of NFTs' future lies in this tokenization boom, as there are some examples of people trading unique real-world assets as NFTs.

"NFT technology is really about ownership," he states. "They describe the ownership of a specific asset that could be a digital asset or real-world asset." He says things like real-estate contracts, expensive watches, artworks or luxury sports cars can now be tokenized, with NFTs created to represent these physical objects.

That immediately begs the question: Why would anyone want to have a digital, NFT version of their watch or sports car?

"Some people want to just speculate on the value of the physical asset and for them, it's great that you don't need to move the physical object around," Barbon mentioned.

"If the object is a nice painting and you buy it from the US, you want to ship it to the UK, that's very costly, it's hassle and it's potentially not safe if the value of this painting is very high," he explained.

He says some companies, such as Courtyard.io, keep physical vaults to hold physical assets which are traded online as NFTs. He says very often, the owner has no interest in having physical possession of the asset.

In a recent development, another area where he sees some promise for the future of NFTs is connected to artificial intelligence. He says NFTs could help with AI safety, as they could be used to provide unique, verifiable, non-fungible identities for AI agents.

Ethereum and other blockchain providers are in the process of trying to build NFT systems that would represent and verify AI agents, something Barbon indicates could be very successful.

He envisages a scenario where AI agents are recorded on an NFT blockchain and can then be identified and rated for safety and reliability.

It has been revealed that "Everybody else can then see that the AI agent is actually doing well, you can trust it, it's safe," he says. "In order to do that, you need something which is uniquely attached to each AI agent and that can be an NFT.".

Another possible use he sees for NFTs in the AI era is that writers and artists could tokenize their work as NFTs so that if an AI agent ends up using it for training, the original work can be more easily identified as unique to the creator.

"Maybe you could then claim that the AI company has to pay you because they have used your content," Barbon notes.

While the NFT craze of 2021 can now be seen as a classic bubble, many of those who invested in it have moved on to memecoins and other forms of fungible cryptocurrency, according to Ben Charoenwong.

"Overall, I think the market did not reject blockchains; it rejected non-fungibility," he states.

At the time of the craze, Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates mentioned NFT popularity was "100% based on the greater fool theory," the idea being that one can make money through the purchase of overvalued, fundamentally worthless assets as long as there is a"greater fool" willing to pay even more.

According to recent reports, one of the most famous NFT collections was the Bored Ape Yacht Club, a series of drawings of apes in various locations in various states of boredom. "Obviously, expensive digital images of monkeys are going to improve the world immensely," Gates joked.

Recent findings suggest that in many ways, that collection's current status epitomizes NFTs' fall from grace better than anything else. Although it remains one of the biggest NFT marketplaces, its value has plunged.

It has been revealed that the singer Justin Bieber bought one image for 500 ETH (Ethereum), or around $1.3 million dollars. The value fell by around 99% to around $14,000. He still owns it.

According to recent reports, yet the fact that these images still command such prices demonstrates they are not entirely worthless. That offers some hope to those who still believe in the technology. Alongside other possible applications linked to AI and tokenization, NFTs may still have a future, albeit a more modest one than when they first came to public attention.

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho gave a strong response when asked about the potential that Endrick could leave.

In the past few days, it has been reported that Endrick could leave Los Blancos in the January transfer window. Not only that, but Real Madrid are apparently opening up to the idea of a permanent sale, with sources in Brazil stating that Milan are ready to offer a €70m package to get him.

There have also been indications that the Spanish giants want to include a buy-back clause of €80m (as they did with Como for Nico Paz in the summer), but in amongst all of this Mourinho seems to be the one opposing any kind of exit for the 20-year-old.

Mourinho spoke at a press conference and he was asked about about the future of Endrick, admitting that the decision to let him leave may come from his superiors. MilanNews relayed his response.

Sources indicate that “I love Endrick, and Real Madrid are more notable than him. We need Endrick here and Real Madrid coach needs Endrick here,” he began.

Recent findings suggest that “This is the answer to those who write things and agents. Then if the club decides other things, I respect that. But for me, as Real Madrid coach, Endrick is important. I need him.”.

The ‘agents’ that Mourinho is referring to could well be Endrick’s entourage, who have given comments suggesting that a move is being explored, while they reportedly visited Milano in recent days too.

Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction.
  • Sources indicate that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.
  • Industry observers note that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

Sources indicate that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

Industry observers note that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

The Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews remarked. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

Sources indicate that brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

Industry observers note that to play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak said. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very notable points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola stated they will now be out “for some time”.

According to recent reports, the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” said Iraola.

It has been revealed that the injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their significant-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Speaking to Sky Sports after his first Premier League win as Fulham head coach, Arbeloa said: “I’m so happy, happy for my players, happy for my supporters, happy for everyone at the club that they deserve this victory. We [waited] a lot of time and some many games that I think we deserved this victory before, but today we did a very good game and yes, I can’t believe that the game finished just 1-0.”.

Brentford head coach Keith Andrews has revealed Aaron Hickey and Nathan Collins will be out for a "number of weeks".

Hickey was forced off with a hamstring injury in the first half of Scotland's 4-0 defeat against Switzerland in Monday's UEFA Nations League encounter.

The full-back, who has a history of hamstring problems, is now set for a spell on the sidelines along with Nathan Collins, who missed the Republic of Ireland's 3-0 win over Kosovo with a knee issue.

“No, they won't be available for a number of weeks,” Andrews said when he spoke to reporters ahead of Monday's Premier League meeting with Everton.

“I was actually watching Aaron's game as it happened and I'm just so bitterly disappointed for him.

“He's had such a painful journey on that front with injury, so it's really disappointing for him.

In a recent development, “Similarly with Nathan, he's obviously had a period out with his calf. He's done really well to get back ahead of schedule and played a couple of games.

Sources indicate that “These international games came at a really good time for him to get good game time and obviously represent his country, and unfortunately he's hurt his knee. Nathan will be out for a couple of weeks or so.”.

Brentford are also without the first-choice striker Igor Thiago, who will serve a three-match ban after being sent off in the 2-0 defeat to Brighton & Hove Albion before the international window.

The Bees are also without the injured duo of Rico Henry and Kaye Furo, while Josh Dasilva and Antoni Milambo are not ready to return to first-team action despite making progress in their respective recoveries.

In positive news, Andrews has revealed Fabio Carvalho has "every chance" of featuring in Monday's squad after missing the last four games through injury.

Brentford head into the weekend in eighth place in the Premier League table, but they are not in the best of form after winning just one of their last five league games.

#37368. Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1701 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

Germany's celebrated children's author Janosch has died

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that janosch, the pen name of German author and illustrator Horst Eckert, won hearts around the world with his warm and simple sense of humor. He charmed children and adults alike with his iconic Tiger, Bear, Tiger-Duck and other animals.

Janosch created more than 150 books, which have been translated into over 30 languages.

According to recent reports, his best-selling children's book, "Oh, wie schön ist Panama," translated into English as "The Trip to Panama," was so lucrative that Janosch was able to settle down on the Canary Island of Tenerife in 1980, where he lived together with his wife Ines. The writer and illustrator died peacefully at the age of 95, his publisher Bernhard Feil announced on Wednesday.

In a recent development, janosch was born as Horst Eckert on March 11, 1931, in Hindenburg (now Zabrze, Poland) in what was then Upper Silesia. After World War II, his family had to flee to Germany.

In 1953, Janosch started studying at the Academy of Art in Munich, thinking that it would be easy to become an artist. He was however dismissed after just a few terms for "lack of talent.".

But luckily for his later readers, Janosch did not give up. He continued to work as a freelance artist, soon discovering his second great gift, namely writing.

His first children's book about a horse named Valek was published in 1960.

Although Janosch became famous primarily for his children's books, he also wrote books for adults that focused on his own childhood.

Even though he wrote cheerful books for children, Janosch hardly had any positive memories of his own childhood, as his father was an alcoholic. He was beaten not only by him but also by his mother and grandmother. Raised in a strictly Catholic environment, he was continuously threatened to be punished by God.

Later on, Janosch tried to overcome the burden of his childhood memories by turning to alcohol as well.

Recent findings suggest that he always expressed a great deal of understanding for children, trying to encourage them to stand up for their rights. As a result of his childhood experiences, Janosch did not want to have children himself, and his attitude towards the Catholic Church always remained divided. "As I am a sinner and a heretic, God will let me live a long life so that I can return to the Church," he told his biographer Angela Bajorek.

Janosch's animal figures are endearing but not always well-behaved. They love all kinds of nonsense. But even if they lie to each other or put their own interests first, the true winner at the end of stories is always friendship and solidarity.

Industry observers note that janosch achieved his major breakthrough with "The Trip to Panama," a story about two friends, a little tiger and a bear, who set out to find their paradise in Panama. After touring around in circles, they finally end up where they started out; they realize that their journey was the destination. Janosch received the German Youth Book Prize in 1979 for the work.

Janosch's protagonists have become familiar to generations of children all over the world. They come up over and over again in the various stories carefully illustrated with water colors.

There is the honest lion Hans from the toy chest who fails to catch a nutcracker with his lies. There is Schnuddel and a ridiculous bragger Günter the Box-Frog. And then there is a tiger that collects mushrooms while looking out for his devoted friend, a bear, who always stands up for him even when the tiger temporarily leaves him because of a little pig in one of the stories.

The "Tigerente," literally "Tiger-Duck," a wooden duck on wheels with yellow-brown stripes, appears on numerous pictures by the illustrator. At times, the animal has been tossed into a corner, at times it is hanging from the ceiling, or the Box-Frog pulls it across the drawing.

Industry observers note that his iconic figures, especially the Tiger-Duck, have served as motifs on various items, from cups to stamps to jewelry, and even on airplanes. Film adaptations and TV series based on his stories were produced in German and English.

Guests who visited Janosch in Tenerife were impressed by his very modest lifestyle. He always noted that hanging around in his hammock doing nothing was what he enjoyed most. And yet Janosch remained very active until the end of his life.

Sources indicate that from 2013 to 2019, he wrote a column for the German weekly Die Zeit, taking on the role of Mr. Wondrak, who commented on world affairs. Shortly before his 90th birthday in 2021, the complete collection of his Mr. Wondrak columns were published as a book in German.

Like the protagonists in his stories, Janosch always tried to content himself with few things. As he wrote in one of his books: "He who needs almost nothing, has everything.".

Sources indicate that luciano Spalletti struck a defiant tone on the eve of Juventus-Napoli, a game seen as a must-win. He also backed the club's response to the defeat at Genoa, including a squad retreat.

Spalletti made his stance clear on the eve of Juventus-Napoli. Anyone expecting him to retreat even slightly, he warned, should expect something different.

Industry observers note that sunday’s game is at the Allianz Stadium. Spalletti noted the side want to win back the respect that has been taken from them. Several outlets say his job is on the line.

The build-up has been shaped by the club’s response to the defeat at Genoa. Ehizibue scored in the 12th minute and Baldanzi in the 28th. After a long meeting between chief executive Giovanni Carnevali and the squad, Spalletti revealed a retreat. The team would stay at the Continassa from Friday evening until the Napoli game.

Spalletti called Carnevali’s address perfect and said he had hit the right notes. He has never been keen on training-camp retreats. In these circumstances, though, he said one could help the group become more compact again.

The coach also played down any need for public backing. He needs no reassurance from the club, only a reaction from the team, Eurosport reported. He added that he is not asking his players for anything beyond their capabilities.

Recent findings suggest that after nine rounds, this season’s tally trails the 15 Juventus had at the same stage last season and the 17 under Motta in 2024/25. It is above the 13 under Allegri in 2022/23, according to Tuttosport.

Sources indicate that recent form has been uneven. The last five league results were a 2-0 home win over Atalanta, a 1-1 draw at Cagliari and a 3-0 home defeat by Lazio. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50.
  • ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.
  • Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 20 Nov 2026 19:45, Last updated: 20 Nov 2026 19:50.

ADO Den Haag travel to the Johan Cruyff Arena on Sunday, looking to end their six-match losing run against Amsterdam giants Ajax in this weekend's matchday 13 Eredivisie encounter.

Their 15-year wait for victory in this fixture further underlines the magnitude of the task facing Maurice Steijn's side.

Ajax entered the recent international break wondering what might have been after surrendering a two-goal advantage at FC Twente.

Goals from Tolu Arokodare and substitute Rayane Bounida seemingly put Michel's men home and hosed heading into the final half-hour, only for Dies Janse to score an own goal and Wout Weghorst to punish his former side with a penalty in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

That equaliser denied De Joden the opportunity to finish gameweek 12 atop the Eredivisie table, leaving them level on 25 points with Feyenoord and one behind leaders PSV Eindhoven, who are chasing a fourth consecutive title.

Looking to move on from that setback, the Amsterdam giants welcome ADO to the capital aiming to secure a seventh consecutive victory over the promoted side.

Further encouraging the hosts is their longstanding unbeaten record in this fixture, with a 3-2 defeat in March 2011 marking Ajax's last loss to this weekend's visitors.

ADO have since gone 20 competitive meetings without a victory in this fixture, losing 15 times to underline their historical inferiority.

As such, it will be intriguing to see how upcoming boss Steijn approaches his first match in charge of the promoted side, who dismissed Robin Peter before the international break following a run of one victory in 11 Eredivisie matches.

There was an immediate lift under Levi Schwiebbe as the second-bottom outfit defeated Sparta Rotterdam 3-1 to move within one point of 16th-placed Telstar in the relegation playoff spot and two of SBV Excelsior.

Back-to-back top-flight victories could therefore lift Den Haag out of the relegation positions, although results elsewhere must also go their way.

Despite the managerial change, ADO's away record offers little encouragement, with the visitors collecting just two points from an available 18 on their travels and failing to score in three of those six matches.

Those figures, coupled with their historical struggles against Ajax, underline the challenge facing Steijn, who is winless in 15 previous encounters with the capital club, losing 11.

ADO Den Haag form (all competitions):.

Ajax could again be without Julian Brandt this weekend, with the attacking midfielder having not played since going off injured in late October's 1-0 victory over AZ Alkmaar.

If the six-goal Germany international remains sidelined, Arokodare, who has seven goals and one assist, will shoulder much of the attacking responsibility, while Oscar Gloukh offers a creative threat with six assists, including setting up both goals in the 2-2 draw at Twente a fortnight ago.

While Anton Gaaei, like Brandt, will be assessed before Sunday, Michel must manage without Simon Adingra, long-term absentee Kasper Dolberg (knee) and Viktor Tsygankov.

Steijn has fewer injury concerns, although the ADO boss must make do without Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl (groin) this weekend.

Juho Kilo may not score regularly, but the midfielder's passing and creativity make him a standout presence for the visitors.

Nonetheless, the goalscoring burden falls on Nigel Thomas, Yannick Eduardo and Evan Rottier, who have netted four, three and two league goals respectively.

Ter Stegen; Rosa, Bouman, Janse, Wijndal; Amrabat, Baas; Klaassen, Mokio, Gloukh; Arokodare.

ADO Den Haag possible starting lineup:.

Nikiema; De Ruijter, Mulder, Waem, Hokke; Kilo, Jimenez; Van Mieghem, Rottier, Hawkins; Thomas.

Ajax's late collapse at Twente demonstrated that their defensive concentration remains fallible, offering some hope to an ADO side fresh from scoring three against Sparta.

Nevertheless, Gloukh's creativity and Arokodare's finishing should give Michel's men enough attacking quality to overcome Brandt's potential absence and prolong the visitors' miserable record in this fixture.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.
  • Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW noted.
  • Recent findings suggest that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

German carmaker BMW reported a nearly 15% drop in third-quarter net profit on Wednesday, as competition from China shakes the global car industry.

Net profit for the third quarter fell to 1.45 billion euros ($1.61 billion), while sales fell nearly 6% to 30.45 billion euros, BMW noted.

Recent findings suggest that the main cause of the decline was BMW's poor business in China. Although the firm sold more cars in the US and Europe compared to the same period last year, this could only partially offset the decline in China.

BMW's car deliveries in China, which were already at their lowest level since 2017 last year, fell 24.8% in the quarter and consequently dragged global deliveries down by 6.3.

CEO Milan Nedeljkovic stated his company would "specifically intensify and accelerate structural measures.".

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

BMW on Tuesday also lowered its outlook for the current year, citing the faster-than-planned implementation of restructuring measures that includes 8,000 layoffs in its home market.

German carmakers have been struggling to compete with their Chinese counterparts in the electric vehicle market,  resulting in cost-cutting measures.

Volkswagen, the world's second-largest carmaker, is battling mounting competition from falling demand in its core Chinese market.

BMW, and its industry heavyweight peers, Volkswagen and Mercedes-Benz, have announced prepares to scale back production and reduce costs.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The Volkswagen Group posted its worst quarterly results in more than a decade earlier this October.

It is looking to cut about 15% of its workforce worldwide, or 100,000 jobs, by the end of the decade. BMW has announced that it will cut up to 8,000 jobs — about 5% of its workforce — by the end of 2027.

On the other hand, German auto parts supplier Schaeffler confirmed on Tuesday that it planned to cut almost 3,500 jobs and close five sites in Europe, by 2028.

According to the manufacturer statement, three-fourths of the 3,460 job cuts and four of the five site closures will be in Germany.

German automotive supplier Bosch, the world's biggest, revealed last year that it would cut 13,000 jobs, mostly in its auto division.

Industry observers note that juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

Industry observers note that the result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

It has been revealed that napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

It has been revealed that spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

In a recent development, napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

It has been revealed that sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win vital for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR.

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026.

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, newcastle United look like a poor team playing badly. The evidence is increasingly damning after Matthias Jaissle’s side were loudly booed off at the end of this limp defeat.

This has all the makings of a long, hard season. Anger is already rising to the surface, even though Jaissle claimed Newcastle deserved more from a game they “controlled” in the first half and “dominated” in the second. Those comments jarred with what we had just seen.

After four years of enjoying an upward trajectory under Eddie Howe, the team faded last season, sold their best players in the summer, lost the manager and there is no evidence yet they have replaced anything with better.

This was supposed to be a reaction to the embarrassing 4-1 thrashing at Coventry City, but it led to another loss and, in the first half at least, another abject display. Aston Villa were always the more fluent and more threatening. They should have won by more than just Johan Manzambi’s first-half header.

According to recent reports, johan Manzambi heads Aston Villa in front! 🟣 https://t.co/jxZf2568Sl.

It is getting hard to comprehend what Jaissle wants his team to do. The much-hyped “vertical” style looks like an ugly incarnation of the long ball football of yesteryear. They did not like it at Newcastle in the 1980s and 1990s and some fashions should never return. It is in danger of resembling a shell suit that has emerged from the back of the wardrobe for a Saturday night out.

There is so much confidence in the German in the Newcastle boardroom that they believe improvement is inevitable, but that is far from assured. Newcastle are not getting better; they are making all the same mistakes and, if anything, as an attacking force, they are looking increasingly stale and predictable. They did not have a shot on target in the first half and, other than one fantastic save in the second, Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki had nothing to do.

"If he doesn't slip Harvey Barnes in, he's got to hit the target" Shay Given discusses Newcastle's decision-making in the final third 🔲 https://t.co/wh4kCAEbxV.

It is time for a sharp dose of medicine on Tyneside. Expectations need to be adjusted, especially as none of the newly introduced signings have impressed. This was always the fear and the risk when you put all your faith in young players from abroad.

For Jaissle’s vertical football to work, Newcastle need to be able to win the ball high up the pitch, whether that is with a high press or competing for second balls from long passes. They do not do either well. More worryingly, they look so vulnerable, so easy to play through.

Industry observers note that villa did it to them all afternoon. Nicolas Jackson should have scored in the first half, Ibrahim Mbaye should have hit the target in the second.

On another day, Newcastle could also have had centre-back Sven Botman sent off for a lunge on Jackson. Then it really would have become ugly, but the Dutchman survived a VAR check.

Recent findings suggest that villa were always the better side. There was no fluency in Newcastle’s game, no structure, no patterns of play. Every time they turned over the ball, they looked stretched. Every time they got a set-piece, it was defended easily. Every time they went forward in the first half, the ball was sent aimlessly long and came straight back at them. In the second, they huffed and puffed but did not sustain any pressure on the Villa goal. The missed chances late on were not clear opportunities and they were snatched at by the hapless Yoane Wissa.

It has been revealed that the home crowd tried to remain patient and supportive, but the sight of yet another long, aimless ball being punted forward straight to a Villa defender tipped some over the edge. There were boos and jeers in the stands while Jaissle screamed at Joe Willock and Wissa. There were more boos at half-time; things felt combustible.

Newcastle needed a substantial second half. They were better, but it was hardly anything to get excited about. A shot on the turn from Botman, superbly saved by Suzuki. Then a few half-chances were squandered, the occasional flash of a threat and that was it.

'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said in a statement on Wednesday that the impact of last week's Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) decision requiring it to reinstate Russia to international play had been "significantly underestimated.".

It added that it "maintains" its disagreement with the decision and that it remained "in dialogue with Member National Associations, organizing committees, host authorities and other key stakeholders to determine the best way forward.".

Shortly after Russia introduced its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the IIHF barred its teams from competing in international ice hockey tournaments, citing security concerns. In last Friday's ruling, the CAS said that the IIHF's concerns were "not supported by sufficient evidence.".

Wednesday's statement comes after two days of talks by the IIHF Council aimed at charting a way forward following Friday's CAS decision, which appears to have caught most of the international ice hockey community off guard.

Two of the organizing committees the statement refers to are those of Canada, which is due to host the IIHF World Junior Championship starting next month, and Germany, which is to host the IIHF Men's World Championship next May. Both countries are strong supporters of Ukraine in its war against Russia, and both have expressed serious reservations about their upcoming tournaments in light of the CAS ruling.

On Tuesday, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney ruled out allowing Russians to compete in the World Juniors in Alberta.

"While Russia and Belarus are supporting this illegal, unjustified ​war in Ukraine, as long as that's going on, there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada," he told reporters at a press conference in Antigua, where he was attending a Commonwealth meeting.

"So, ​if you're asking specifically about the World Juniors, the Russians will not be there.".

Last weekend, Frank Lutz, chairman of the German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) conceded in a television interview that following the CAS decision, the DEB would "also have to consider the option of handing back (hosting rights to) this championship.".

In a statement to DW on Wednesday, a German government spokesperson reiterated Berlin's position on the matter from the weekend, saying it viewed Friday's CAS ruling "very critically.".

The spokesperson also said  the government would "consult with the German Ice Hockey Federation in the near future regarding the potential consequences of this decision, including its impact on the 2027 Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany.".

Meanwhile, the ice hockey association of Finland, the defending men's world champions, has been spearheading an effort to boycott upcoming IIHF tournaments should the Russians be allowed to compete.

"We are currently working to bring as many countries as possible into a united front to tell the IIHF that none of us will play against Russia under these circumstances," Finnish Ice Hockey Association boss Heikki Hietanen stated in a statement released on the organization's website on Monday.

"Our stance is that we will not play against Russia as long as the war of aggression against Ukraine continues," added Hietanen, who is also a member of the IIHF Council.

Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Czechia have since made similar statements.

"The Three Crowns will not play Russia in coming world championship tournaments," Swedish Ice Hockey Federation boss Anders Larsson said.

This came shortly after Norway mentioned it would not play Russia at the Men's World Championship and the Danish Ice Hockey Federation issued a similar statement on its website.

Sources indicate that "Denmark will – based on the current situation and the information available to us today – not play against Russia at the World Championship in Germany in May 2027," it read. Denmark did not qualify for the World Juniors.

Czechia Ice Hockey Association President Alois Hadamczik confirmed on Tuesday that they too would refrain from playing Russian teams.

Latvia's federation said it “reaffirms its longstanding and firm position" not to play against Russia or its ally Belarus.

Alexander Helwig, chairman of the Austrian Ice Hockey Association told public broadcaster ORF that “as of now, we would certainly not play against Russia.".

USA Hockey has yet to comment on the CAS ruling.

According to recent reports, at the same time, sponsors of IIHF tournaments are also getting cold feet. Skoda, which has been the main sponsor of the Men's World Championship for more than three decades, told the Associated Press that it would "reassess" its position if Russia takes part.

In a recent development, "We do not support the Court of Arbitration for Sport's decision regarding the participation of Russian national teams in IIHF competitions. With Russia's aggression continuing, we believe the Russian national team's return to the world championship is incompatible with the values we have consistently upheld," the Czech carmaker said.

Skoda isn't alone either, Finnish tire manufacturer Nokian had mentioned it would end its backing if Russia took part and Swedish furniture maker AJ Products, whose logo has been seen on the boards and officials' jerseys at World Championships since 1989, said Monday it would ask for its logo not to be shown.

On Wednesday afternoon, yet another sponsor joined the list, with German workwear company Strauss saying it would "forgo all logo exposure associated with the (men's) tournament" and was considering withdrawing its sponsporship entirely.

With the IIHF Council having failed to agree on how to proceed during its meetings on Monday and Tuesday, President Franz Reindl told Germany's SID news agency on Wednesday, that it would reconvene for further talks on Thursday.

According to recent reports, this article was originally published on November 4, 2026. It was updated on November 5, 2026 with the German government statement to DW.
